concepts.title: From Self to Family: The Widening Lens

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'From Self to Family: The Widening Lens' refers to.
questions.a: Unit II turns the discipline's lens outward: having understood the adolescent self, it now studies the family -- the first and most enduring institution -- and the community and society in which families are embedded and by which they are shaped.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'From Self to Family: The Widening Lens'.
questions.a: The self is the starting point; family, community and society are the widening circles it lives within.

questions.q: Under which section is 'From Self to Family: The Widening Lens' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: The Family as the Basic Institution

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Family as the Basic Institution' refers to.
questions.a: The family is humanity's basic social institution: it bears and rears children, transmits culture and values, and provides economic and emotional support. Its forms vary -- nuclear, joint, extended, single-parent -- but its functions of care, socialisation and support remain central to every society.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Family as the Basic Institution'.
questions.a: First school, first economy, first refuge -- the family performs society's most intimate functions.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Family as the Basic Institution' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: unit (source: kehe107.txt unit opener and family sections (family as basic institution, functions of family, types of family, care and support))

concepts.title: Community and Society as Frameworks of Family Life

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Community and Society as Frameworks of Family Life' refers to.
questions.a: Families never live alone: neighbourhoods, schools, workplaces and services form the community, and larger social structures -- laws, economy, culture -- form society. Understanding family life therefore means reading these frameworks, from community resources to social expectations, that support or strain the household.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Community and Society as Frameworks of Family Life'.
questions.a: Behind every family stand its community's services and society's rules -- read them to read the family.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Community and Society as Frameworks of Family Life' taught, and from which source text?
